paragraphs.notes: Continuation fragment. The page body is one uninterrupted comma-separated list of substituent group names running on from page 14 and continuing onto page 16; no sentence starts or ends on this page and no paragraph number is printed anywhere in this patent, so marker is null. The list is transcribed as one running string: where a name is broken across a line end by the printed hyphen that is part of the name (Dialkylsulfonyl-N- / alkyl-amino, Cycloalkenyl-alkinylsulfonyl-N-alkyl- / amino, Heterocyclyl-alkinylsulfonyl-N-alkyl- / amino) the two halves are rejoined without adding or removing a character. en is identical to zh: the entries are chemical substituent-group names, not German prose. They carry German orthography (Alkinyl, Cycloalkenyl, Heterocyclyl) and were NOT respelled to the English forms (alkynyl, heterocyclyl) because respelling would silently normalise the verbatim record; the German-to-English difference here is spelling only. Printed as-is and deliberately not corrected: 'Dialkylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino' where the series pattern would give Alkylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino; a lowercase initial on 'cycloalkenylalkenylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino' where every neighbouring entry is capitalised; 'Heterocyclylalkyl, Heterocyclylalkenyl, Heterocyclylalkinyl' in the middle of the -carbonyl series, where the pattern would give Heterocyclylalkylcarbonyl and so on; and a jump from 'Cycloalkylcarbonyloxy' straight to 'Cycloalkylalkenylcarbonyloxy' with no Cycloalkylalkylcarbonyloxy between them. The hyphenation of the -sulfonyl- entries is also inconsistent as printed (Arylalkylsulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino beside Heteroarylalkyl-sulfonyl-N-alkyl-amino) and is reproduced exactly. A small ink speck sits just below the 'l' of 'Dialkylsulfonyl' on line 3; it is scanner dirt, not a character, and obscures nothing.
